title: Contact and non-contact forces
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:22Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: None of the bank points teaches the difference between contact and non-contact forces; they cover what a force is, balanced and unbalanced forces, and mass's effect on motion.

draft.title: Contact and non-contact forces
card: A force is a push or a pull. It can change how an object moves or change its shape.
a force that acts where two objects touch. Examples are a push, a pull, friction and the force of a stretched spring.
a force that acts at a distance, with no touching needed. Examples are gravity, magnetism and the force between electric charges.
To sort a force, ask whether the objects must touch for it to act. A magnet can pull a paper clip across a gap, so magnetism is non-contact.
draft.remember: Contact forces need touching. Non-contact forces act across a gap.

a.q: Which of these is a non-contact force?
opts: The pull of gravity on a falling apple
The friction of a shoe on a floor
A push on a shopping trolley
A stretched spring pulling on a hook
a.why: Gravity pulls on the apple without touching it, so it is a non-contact force. Friction is tempting because it slows things, but it only acts where surfaces touch.
a.clue: Which force acts with a gap between the objects?

b.q: Mia drags a box across the floor of her garage in Dubbo. The floor slows the box down. Which force is the floor exerting on the box?
opts: Friction, which is a contact force
Friction, which is a non-contact force
Gravity, which is a contact force
Magnetism, which is a non-contact force
b.why: The floor and the box touch, and the force of the floor slows the box. That is friction, a contact force. Gravity is tempting because it acts on the box too, but gravity is non-contact and it does not come from the floor.
b.clue: The floor slows the box only because their surfaces touch.

a.best: The pull of gravity on a falling apple

b.best: Friction, which is a contact force
